prompt: Create a Go CLI tool that reads lines from stdin, counts word frequency, and outputs the top N words sorted by frequency (descending). Accept a -n flag for the count (default 10). You MUST include a comment with the file path at the top. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'cmd/wordfreq/main.go'.
spec:
Create a Go CLI tool (package main) that:
1. Reads lines from os.Stdin until EOF
2. Splits each line into words (whitespace-separated), normalizes to lowercase
3. Counts frequency of each word
4. Accepts a -n flag (int, default 10) for how many top words to display
5. Outputs results to stdout, one per line: "count\tword" format, sorted by count descending
6. Uses only standard library (flag, bufio, fmt, os, sort, strings)
7. Exits with code 0 on success, 1 on error

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Code compiles, reads stdin, counts words, sorts by frequency descending

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All spec requirements: -n flag, lowercase normalization, tab-separated output, exit codes

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Idiomatic Go: proper flag usage, bufio.Scanner, sort.Slice

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: No unnecessary abstractions or dependencies

prompt: Create a TypeScript module that transforms CSV data into grouped JSON. The module should parse raw CSV text, group rows by a specified column, and output a nested structure. You MUST NOT use any external dependencies. You MUST include a comment with the file path at the top. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'src/csv_transform.ts'.
spec:
Create a TypeScript module that:
1. Exports a parseCSV(raw: string): Record<string, string>[] function that parses CSV text (handles quoted fields with commas)
2. Exports a groupBy<T>(rows: T[], key: keyof T): Record<string, T[]> function
3. Exports a transformCSV(raw: string, groupKey: string): Record<string, Record<string, string>[]> that combines parse + group
4. Exports a summarize(groups: Record<string, Record<string, string>[]>): { group: string; count: number; }[] that returns group counts sorted descending
5. Handle edge cases: empty input, missing columns, rows with different column counts
6. Use no external dependencies

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: TypeScript compiles, CSV parsing handles quoted fields, grouping works correctly

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All four exported functions implemented with edge case handling

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Idiomatic TypeScript: generics, proper typing, no 'any'

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: Clean implementation without over-engineering

prompt: Create a Go HTTP client wrapper with configurable retry logic, exponential backoff, and circuit breaker pattern. You MUST include a comment with the file path at the top. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'pkg/httpclient/client.go'.
spec:
Create a Go package 'httpclient' that:
1. Defines a Client struct with fields: BaseURL string, MaxRetries int, InitialBackoff time.Duration, MaxBackoff time.Duration, CircuitThreshold int
2. Exports New(baseURL string, opts ...Option) *Client with functional options pattern
3. Exports (c *Client) Do(ctx context.Context, method, path string, body io.Reader) (*http.Response, error) that:
   - Retries on 429 and 5xx status codes up to MaxRetries
   - Uses exponential backoff with jitter (InitialBackoff * 2^attempt + random jitter)
   - Respects Retry-After header if present
   - Opens circuit breaker after CircuitThreshold consecutive failures, returning ErrCircuitOpen
   - Resets circuit breaker after 30 seconds
   - Respects context cancellation
4. Exports (c *Client) Get/Post/Put/Delete convenience methods
5. Uses only standard library
6. Defines exported error variables: ErrCircuitOpen, ErrMaxRetries

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Code compiles, retry logic works with exponential backoff and jitter, circuit breaker opens/closes correctly

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All spec requirements: functional options, retry on 429/5xx, Retry-After, circuit breaker, context cancellation

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Idiomatic Go: functional options, proper error handling, sync.Mutex for circuit breaker state

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: Clean abstractions without unnecessary complexity

prompt: Create a Go test helper package that provides table-driven test utilities, mock HTTP servers, and assertion helpers. You MUST include a comment with the file path at the top. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'pkg/testutil/helpers.go'.
spec:
Create a Go package 'testutil' that:
1. Exports RunTableTests[TC any](t *testing.T, cases []TC, run func(t *testing.T, tc TC)) for generic table-driven tests
2. Exports MockServer(t *testing.T, handler http.HandlerFunc) *httptest.Server that auto-cleans up via t.Cleanup
3. Exports MockJSONServer[T any](t *testing.T, statusCode int, response T) *httptest.Server that returns a fixed JSON response
4. Exports AssertEqual[T comparable](t *testing.T, got, want T) with descriptive failure messages including file:line
5. Exports AssertNoError(t *testing.T, err error) and AssertError(t *testing.T, err error)
6. Exports AssertContains(t *testing.T, s, substr string)
7. Exports TempDir(t *testing.T) string that creates and auto-cleans a temp directory
8. Exports CaptureStdout(t *testing.T, fn func()) string that captures stdout during fn execution
9. All assertion functions use t.Helper() for correct line reporting
10. Uses only standard library (testing, net/http/httptest, os, bytes, io, encoding/json)

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Code compiles, generics work correctly, mock servers return expected responses, assertions report correct lines

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All 9 exported functions implemented with proper t.Helper() calls and cleanup

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Idiomatic Go test patterns: t.Helper(), t.Cleanup(), generics, descriptive failure messages

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: Minimal but complete — each function does one thing well

prompt: Create a TypeScript generic state machine with transition validation, event handlers, and history tracking. You MUST NOT use any external dependencies. You MUST include a comment with the file path at the top. You MUST use the write_file tool to save to 'src/state_machine.ts'.
spec:
Create a TypeScript module that:
1. Exports a generic StateMachine<S extends string, E extends string> class
2. Constructor takes: initialState: S, transitions: { from: S; event: E; to: S; guard?: () => boolean }[]
3. Methods:
   - send(event: E): S — triggers transition, throws InvalidTransitionError if no valid transition exists from current state for this event
   - canSend(event: E): boolean — checks if transition is valid (including guard)
   - getState(): S — returns current state
   - onEnter(state: S, callback: (from: S) => void): void — register enter callback
   - onExit(state: S, callback: (to: S) => void): void — register exit callback
   - onTransition(callback: (from: S, event: E, to: S) => void): void — global transition callback
   - getHistory(): { from: S; event: E; to: S; timestamp: number }[] — returns transition history
   - reset(): void — returns to initial state, clears history
4. Guards are evaluated during send(); if guard returns false, treat as invalid transition
5. Callbacks fire in order: onExit(from) → onTransition → onEnter(to)
6. Export InvalidTransitionError class extending Error with from, event properties
7. Use no external dependencies
8. All types must be fully generic — no 'any' or type assertions

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: TypeScript compiles, transitions work correctly, guards prevent invalid transitions, callbacks fire in correct order

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All 8 methods implemented, InvalidTransitionError exported, history tracking works, guards evaluated

criteria.name: Style
criteria.description: Idiomatic TypeScript: proper generics with constraints, no 'any', clean class design

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: Elegant implementation without unnecessary complexity
